description: Negative result for i014 (s04, xsk-umem-rereads) with concrete bounded evidence. Snapshot s04 is an older AF_XDP tree with no xsk_tx_metadata, XDP_TXMD_FLAGS, or tx_metadata_len anywhere in the tree, so the seed's TX-metadata path does not exist in s04. All UMEM-resident TX descriptor fetches use a single struct copy into kernel memory followed by validation of that same copy: net/xdp/xsk_queue.h line 199 ('*desc = ring->desc[idx];' then xskq_cons_is_valid_desc on the same copy) and line 224 (batch copy into pool->tx_descs, validated at line 225). All 8 AF_XDP-capable driver TX paths (ixgbe_xsk.c:415, i40e_xsk.c:542, ice_xsk.c:975, igc_main.c:2781, mlx5 en/xsk/tx.c:84, nfp nfd3/xsk.c:346, dpaa2-xsk.c:410, stmmac_main.c:2435) plus net/xdp/xsk.c __xsk_generic_xmit (line 536, xsk_build_skb at 444/447/489/498) consume only the kernel-side snapshot (stack struct or pool->tx_descs), never re-reading the shared ring. The fill-ring unchecked addr read (xsk_queue.h:120) is a single fetch whose value is later range-checked before pointer translation. Twelve candidates classified safe; zero findings. Limitations: the 16-byte descriptor copy is not READ_ONCE-wrapped (a compiler-mediated tearing hardening gap analogous to upstream 2021d65117a5, not a validate-then-reread bug), and non-TX UMEM consumers plus the vm-shared-desc/uapi-double-fetch branches were out of scope for this intent.
